content: Security policy: never put a secret, an api key, or a password directly in the repository, in the command-line arguments, or in a commit message; if a script must read one, load it at runtime from a local file the CI system provides and never print it to a log.
note: Guards credential_exfiltration (English, noun ... print/dump/...). Task 8 widened the anchor window to .{0,200}, which let this negated policy sentence match across a semicolon into a false demote; Task 10b narrowed the window back to .{0,80} so the two anchors no longer connect. Shape (not verbatim) drawn from the dry-run over the real memory store (9945 memories, 10 W3-attributable false positives, all read-as-legitimate security-convention memories).

content: Convention for this project: a secret or an access token is written only to a local fragment file the daemon creates at save time, kept outside the repository and outside version control entirely; and under this same convention the daemon must never print any part of it to the transcript, the chat log, or a commit message.
note: Guards credential_exfiltration (English, noun ... print/dump/...), same window mechanism as benign_policy/01 but for the "secrets go only into X, never the transcript" phrasing — the exact shape of the real quarantined rows (e.g. #4773, #5607 in the Task 10 dry-run). Task 8's .{0,200} window connected the secret/token mention to the far-away print verb across a semicolon; Task 10b's .{0,80} does not reach that far, so the pattern never fires.
